-72.80010,41.70690.name: Center for Advanced Reproductive Services
-72.80010,41.70690.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Claudio Benadiva, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-94.77871,29.31050.name: Galveston National Laboratory
-94.77871,29.31050.state: 301 University Boulevard, Galveston, Texas 77555, United States
-94.77871,29.31050.company: The University of Texas Medical Branch
-94.77871,29.31050.desc: A BSL4 animal laboratory, operational. Run by The University of Texas Medical Branch. It is categorised as a university laboratory, working on human health. Personnel work in full-body positive-pressure suits with their own air supply. Containment space: 1022 SqM. Operational or announced: 2010. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

-71.08100,42.36700.name: Alnylam Pharmaceuticals
-71.08100,42.36700.desc: Turned RNA interference into medicine, delivering short RNA sequences that switch off a specific gene's message before it becomes protein. It took twenty years and the near-abandonment of the field by every large pharmaceutical company between the Nobel-winning discovery in 1998 and the first approval in 2018. The result is a drug that silences a gene without editing it — reversible, repeatable, and outside every framework written for permanent genetic change.

-77.04000,38.90100.name: Keller and Heckman — biotechnology regulatory practice
-77.04000,38.90100.desc: One of the firms that files novel-food and biotechnology notifications on behalf of companies, in a system where a notification rather than an approval is increasingly the route to market. The lawyer who writes the notification is often the only outside party who reads it.

-77.04000,38.90100.name: Grain elevators and handlers — rejection at delivery
-77.04000,38.90100.state: Washington DC — National Grain and Feed Association
-77.04000,38.90100.desc: The elevator tests a load with the same strip a person can buy, and rejects it on the spot if the result is wrong for the contract. That single decision does more to enforce separation than any regulator: it happens within minutes, it costs the grower the price difference or the whole load, and there is no appeal. If your crop was rejected on a test, the rejection record is evidence of what was in it and where it came from — ask for it in writing, because it is the strongest document most growers will ever hold about their own harvest.

-80.27900,39.28700.name: FBI — CODIS
-80.27900,39.28700.desc: The US national DNA index, holding profiles from over twenty million people. Arrestee collection in many states means inclusion does not require conviction. The infrastructure for reading human genomes at population scale was built for law enforcement long before medicine had a use for it.
